sections.h2: Which two offices deal with property tax in McCreary County?
sections.html:
A parcel's value comes from the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA), and the money goes to the Sheriff. That division holds everywhere in Kentucky, but McCreary County adds a twist: with no incorporated city anywhere inside its lines, there is no city hall tax office and no city levy. County government is the one local government covering every resident.

Mail for the PVA goes to PO Box 609, Whitley City, KY 42653, and the phone is (606) 376-2514 (fax (606) 376-4152). Dial (606) 376-2322 for the Sheriff and (606) 376-2411 for the County Clerk, who records deeds and later takes over bills that stay unpaid. The fiscal court works from 1 North Main Street in Whitley City and holds its public meeting the second Thursday of every month at 6 p.m.

sections.h2: How long does a McCreary County owner have to pay before penalties start?
sections.html:
The assessment date is January 1, the bill falls due by December 31, and the Sheriff keeps collecting until April 15, all under KRS 134.015. Waiting is priced in steps:

  • 2 percent comes off if the full amount is in by November 1.
  • Between November 2 and the last day of December, the printed total applies.
  • Every day of January carries a 5 percent surcharge.
  • February and later bring a 10 percent surcharge.

The 2026 discount date of November 1 has come and gone, so a 2026 bill is now either the printed figure through December 31 or that figure plus a penalty. A bill that survives past April 15 is shifted to the County Clerk as a certificate of delinquency. Two letters from the county attorney follow, and the Clerk must set a sale for a date 90 to 135 days after the shift. A buyer at that sale is free to tack on fees, which is the best reason to settle with the Sheriff beforehand.

sections.h2: What does a McCreary County house cost in tax?
sections.html:
Very little, by Kentucky standards, because values here are low. The Census figure for a typical owned home is $85,300, compared with $188,100 in McCracken County. Applying Frankfort's 2025 rate of 10.6 cents per $100 gives roughly $90.42 of state tax on that house. The fiscal court, the school district and other local bodies set additional rates, and the PVA can total them for a particular address.

No permits were issued in 2025, so new construction adds little to the tax roll, and existing houses make up the market. Wikipedia reports 6,892 housing units at the 2020 census with 12.1 percent vacant, and Census figures show 17.9 percent of residents at 65 or older, the group the state's homestead deduction was written for.

sections.h2: Does McCreary County offer a homestead deduction?
sections.html:
It does, as every Kentucky county must. Owners 65 or older, plus those classed as totally disabled, can have $49,100 knocked off assessed value for 2025 and 2026, and the tax rate is then applied to the balance.

The effect is large here. A house valued at the $85,300 median would be taxed on only $36,200, so the state share falls from about $90.42 to about $38.37. Apply at the PVA office in Whitley City, and show age with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. Disability claims need a federal or retirement-system finding of total disability and yearly renewal, with exceptions for service-connected veterans and for people ruled totally and permanently disabled by Social Security or the Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: What can a McCreary County owner do about an assessment?
sections.html:
Meet the PVA or a deputy first. The state will not take an appeal from someone who skipped that conference, and the PVA is required to lay out how the figure was built. From there:

  • Look over the roll during the 13 days that open on the first Monday in May.
  • File with the County Clerk by the end of the first working day after those 13 days.
  • Attach proof about the land and buildings, such as insurance records, construction costs, comparable sales and photographs. Rural tracts also benefit from a survey. An appeal without papers is denied.
  • Appear before the local board, which sits 25 to 35 days after viewing ends and listens only with both sides in the room.

Skipping the hearing closes the door to the Kentucky Claims Commission. If the board settles above your claimed value after bills were printed, a supplemental bill covers the gap.

sections.h2: What if McCreary County taxes are still owed when the house sells?
sections.html:
The debt rides along with the parcel. KRS 134.015 calls these taxes the owner's personal debt from the assessment date, and the lien described in KRS 134.420 can persist for 11 years, whoever holds title. Once the Clerk has the bill, 1 percent monthly interest accrues, and commissions for the Clerk and the county attorney plus a lien recording fee are added.

Closing agents ask for a payoff before they release funds. Request one from the Sheriff before April 15 and from the Clerk after that date.

sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in McCreary County?
sections.html:
McCreary County is Kentucky's newest, the 120th and last to be formed, cut out of Pulaski, Wayne and Whitley counties in 1912. It spans 431 square miles along the western rim of the Cumberland Plateau, and it is the only county in the state with no incorporated city. Whitley City is the seat, with Pine Knot and Stearns as the other census-designated places. The Daniel Boone National Forest covers about 43 percent of the land and the Big South Fork National River and Recreation Area about 18 percent, which leaves privately owned acreage as a limited share.

Early livelihoods came from timber, coal and the Cincinnati Southern Railway, which arrived in 1880 and fed the Stearns company town. Visitors today come for Cumberland Falls State Park and the Big South Fork Scenic Railway. One school system, McCreary County School District, serves the county, and McCreary Central is its main high school. The county is on Eastern time and counted 17,124 people in 2025, a 1.4 percent gain over 2020.

Workers average 32.3 minutes to reach a job, and 80.1 percent of households subscribe to broadband. The county touches Pulaski, Laurel, Whitley and Wayne counties and two counties in Tennessee. An heir to a house here, or an owner behind on tax, can sell as-is for cash without paying for repairs first.

faqs.q: Is there a city property tax in McCreary County?
faqs.a: No city levy exists, because McCreary is the only Kentucky county without an incorporated city. School and district levies still appear on the bill.

faqs.q: Whom do I pay for McCreary County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Sheriff, at (606) 376-2322, until April 15. The PVA at (606) 376-2514 sets values and takes exemption papers but not money.

faqs.q: How much state tax does an $85,300 McCreary County home owe?
faqs.a: About $90.42, using the 2025 state rate of 10.6 cents per $100. Local rates are charged in addition.

faqs.q: Can a 65-year-old in McCreary County shrink the taxable value?
faqs.a: Yes. The homestead deduction takes $49,100 off assessed value for 2025 and 2026. Bring proof of age to the PVA office.

faqs.q: What if my McCreary County bill moves to the County Clerk?
faqs.a: A recorded lien and 1 percent monthly interest follow. An investor may buy the certificate at a sale held 90 to 135 days after the move.
